item.ultimateponderadditions.guide.toolt: Machines, drawers, chickens and networks, explained.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.ae2_charg: The Charger turns Certus Quartz into Charged Certus Quartz, which is where Fluix comes from.
Drop a crystal in the front and wait. It also recharges tools and energy cells.
No power yet? Bolt a Crank on top and turn it by hand.
The Vibration Chamber burns fuel for AE directly - crude, but it works on day one.
Once you have a real generator, the Energy Acceptor takes over.
Charged Certus plus Nether Quartz plus Redstone, thrown in water, gives you Fluix.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.ae2_craft: A Crafting CPU is any solid cube of crafting blocks attached to the network.
Crafting Storage sets how large a job the CPU can plan. No storage, no crafting.
Co-Processing Units let the CPU push several ingredients out at once.
A Crafting Monitor shows what the CPU is currently working on.
Pattern Providers hold the recipes and push ingredients into the machine behind them.
A Molecular Assembler bolted to a provider handles ordinary crafting-table recipes.
Build several small CPUs rather than one huge one, so separate jobs can run side by side.
Each CPU is one job at a time - the number of CPUs is the number of parallel crafts.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.ae2_growt: Budding Certus Quartz grows crystal buds on its faces, exactly like amethyst does.
The block degrades a tier each time a bud matures: Flawless, Chipped, Damaged, then plain quartz.
Mine a cluster with anything and it drops crystals; mine it with Silk Touch to move the cluster.
Crystal Growth Accelerators touching the block speed the growth up dramatically.
Accelerators need AE power, and they only count when they touch the budding block.
Add a Crystal Resonance Generator and a Spatial IO setup and quartz stops being a bottleneck.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.ae2_inscr: Every AE2 machine is built from processors, and processors come out of Inscribers.
A press goes in the top slot, the material in the middle, and out comes a printed circuit.
Presses are not consumed. Find them in meteorites, or grind Sky Stone until one turns up.
Chain three inscribers together and the last one assembles the printed parts into a processor.
The ME Energy Acceptor converts Forge Energy into AE, which is what the inscriber drinks.
An Energy Cell buffers that power so a burst of crafting does not stall the network.
Once your network has patterns for the presses, a Pattern Provider can drive this whole row.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.ae2_netwo: An ME Network is power, storage, and cable joining them. Everything else is an extra.
Power enters through an ME Energy Acceptor, which converts FE into AE.
The ME Controller hands out channels. Small networks can skip it entirely.
The ME Drive holds storage cells. Each cell is the network's actual disk space.
Every device that stores or moves items eats one channel. A plain cable carries eight.
Terminals, buses and P2P tunnels all attach to the cable as parts.
Run out of channels and devices go dark. Dense cable carries thirty-two instead of eight.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.chickens_: Breeding chickens
The Chicken Breeder takes two chicken items and seeds, and produces offspring.
Both parents have to be ordinary chickens. Roosters do not go in here.
Which chicken you get follows the breeding tree: an Iron and a Flint chicken give Gold.
The Nest is a different machine. It holds a rooster and seeds, and makes no items at all.
What it makes is an aura: while it burns seeds, every Roost in range works faster.
The Mechanical Nest does the same with a Robot Rooster and RF instead of seeds.
Use an Analyzer on a chicken to read its stats before you decide what to pair.
The Henhouse
Chickens dropping resources on the floor need something to pick them up. That is the Henhouse.
It collects nearby chicken drops into a 3x3 inventory inside it.
It runs on FE, or on hay bales as fuel. Burning hay leaves dirt behind as a byproduct.
There is a Henhouse for every wood type, so it matches whatever you built the coop out of.
Cheap and early. A Roost with a Collector is tidier once you can afford it.
The Incubator
The Incubator turns Modern Chickens spawn eggs into the portable chicken items the machines take.
Drop the eggs in and give it power. One conversion takes 200 ticks.
It runs on RF, not on heat. No lava or fire involved.
Chicken items are what Roosts, Breeders and Nests accept, so everything starts here.
An egg out of an Avian Dousing Machine goes straight in here to become the chicken.
The Roost
A Roost holds chicken items and produces their drops into its own output slots. No loose birds.
Chickens in, resources out: iron, redstone, glowstone, whatever that type produces.
Speed and Stack upgrades inside the roost raise how fast and how much it makes.
A Roost Collector pulls the finished output from every Roost in range into its own inventory.
The Mechanical Roost runs on RF and has four independent chicken rows, each with its own output.
A Nest placed nearby projects an aura that speeds up every Roost it reaches.
Power from chickens
Chickens lay more than solid resources. The Avian machines turn the rest into something usable.
The Avian Flux Converter drains Flux Eggs into an FE buffer and pushes it to adjacent machines.
The Avian Fluid Converter cracks Liquid Eggs into a tank and feeds adjacent tanks or pipes.
The Avian Chemical Converter does the same with Chemical and Gas Eggs, into a Mekanism buffer.
The Avian Dousing Machine burns RF plus a reagent to make specialised spawn eggs.
The Roost Generator is the direct route: Redstone Flux Chickens in, FE/t out.
A wall of roosts feeding converters is a serious mid-game power plant.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.fs_armory: Drawers refuse anything with NBT, which rules out tools, armour and enchanted books.
The Armory Cabinet is the answer: hundreds of slots, all happy to hold gear.
One cabinet replaces a very long row of chests.
It is a plain inventory, so hoppers and pipes can fill and empty it as usual.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.fs_compac: A Compacting Drawer stores one material across all of its crafting tiers at once.
Insert iron nuggets, ingots or blocks - the drawer converts between them automatically.
Pull from whichever slot you need. Nine nuggets always come back out as one ingot.
The Simple Compacting Drawer does the same for a single two-step material.
This is the cheapest way to stop nuggets, ingots and blocks eating three separate slots.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.fs_contro: A wall of drawers is only useful if you can search it. That is what the controller is for.
The Storage Controller claims every connected drawer and shows them as one inventory.
Drawers connect through touching faces - the wall has to be one solid piece.
Controller Extensions carry the connection further without adding storage of their own.
Pipes, hoppers and AE2 storage buses can all talk to the controller instead of each drawer.
Out of reach? The Linking Tool binds a distant drawer to the controller by hand.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.fs_drawer: A drawer holds one kind of item per slot, and a lot more of it than a chest would.
One slot: the whole block is a single, very deep stack.
Two and four slot drawers trade capacity for variety.
Right-click a slot to insert one stack, or hold the click to empty your inventory into it.
Left-click a slot to pull one stack back out; sneak-click for one item.
Upgrades go in the drawer's UI: Copper through Netherite raise capacity, Void discards the overflow.
The Configuration Tool locks a drawer to its current item, so it stays reserved when emptied.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.fs_ender_: Two Ender Drawers set to the same frequency are the same drawer, however far apart they sit.
The frequency is a colour code, set in the drawer's UI. Different code, different storage.
Handy for mining trips: one drawer at the dig site, one back at the base.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.if_convey: Conveyors carry dropped items along whichever way they face.
Right-click a conveyor with a wrench to turn it; click the edge to add a ramp.
Run a belt into any inventory and the items insert themselves.
The Block Placer sets blocks from its inventory in front of itself.
The Block Breaker does the opposite, and drops what it mines.
Conveyor upgrades add extraction, insertion, splitting and detection to a belt.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.if_laser_: The Ore Laser Base produces ores out of thin air, powered by Laser Drills around it.
The base sits in the middle. Which ores it can make depends on the dimension it is in.
Every Laser Drill aimed at the base speeds it up. Up to twelve can feed one base.
Put a Laser Lens in a drill to bias the output towards ores of that colour.
The finished ore comes out of the base - pipe it into any inventory you like.
The drills are the hungry part; the base itself needs almost nothing.
A Fluid Laser Base does the same trick for fluids instead of ores.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.if_mob_fa: The Mob Duplicator spawns copies of a mob captured with a Mob Imprisonment Tool.
Fill it with Essence and drop the imprisonment tool in its inventory.
The Mob Crusher kills anything in range and turns it into Essence and drops.
Point the drops at any inventory so nothing despawns.
Crushing mobs produces more Essence than duplicating them costs, so the loop pays for itself.
The Mob Slaughter Factory is the other option: no drops or experience, but Liquid Meat and Pink Slime.
Both killers take Range Addons; a Fortune Addon on the Crusher improves the drops.
ultimateponderadditions.ponder.if_plant_: The Plant Sower and the Plant Gatherer work a 3x3 area in front of them.
The Plant Sower plants whatever seeds you put in its inventory.
It only sows on tilled soil, so till the plot before switching it on.
The Plant Gatherer harvests the same area, and hands the crops out of its back.
A Plant Fertilizer next to the plot speeds the crops along.
Every machine here runs on Forge Energy - no power, no harvest.
Add a Range Addon to each machine to grow the worked area past 3x3.
Every machine here burns Forge Energy, so the first thing to build is a source of it.
The Pitiful Generator burns solid fuel. It is exactly as good as the name suggests, but it starts you off.
The Bioreactor takes plant matter - seeds, saplings, crops - and turns it into Biofuel.
It wants variety: the more distinct plant types in its inventory, the more Biofuel per batch.
The Biofuel Generator burns that Biofuel, and it is in a different league.
The Latex Processing Unit taps trees for Latex, which becomes Tiny Dry Rubber and then Plastic.
The Sludge Refiner turns the Sludge machines produce back into ores and blocks.
Feed the Bioreactor from a Plant Gatherer and the whole factory runs on its own farm.
